findings.reason: §2's one-week re-measure compares the fold's share against 41.9%, so a fold defined otherwise measures an unrelated number and the node's whole gate rests on a mismatch.
findings.text: §9(d) states the second share "is the classification §3 of plan-review cycles uses, read from the reviewed bytes and not from any stored answer", and equates it to the 41.9% baseline; but the research doc's own script derives 41.9% (duplicate_owner 113/270) from the stored response action `== "acted"` on the previous review's same-type finding (`docs/figures/plan-review-cycles/measure_review_cycles.py:609-614`, `.../review-cycles-data.json` q4 `after_acted`=113), not from any unit change — §3's unit-change classification is a separate metric (49.6%, 249/502). Separately, §3 defines a finding as acted when its unit changed between that review and the one before it, so a fold that compares "that review and the next" pins the fold to the wrong interval. A node built to §9(d) computes a different quantity from the 41.9% the fold exists to reproduce
